nodes.title: Generate - stage 2
widgets_values:
## Generate - stage 2

**Upscale and re-sampler (3 steps)**

This subgraph node upscales the result of the first stage by 2 (width & height) and runs another 3 steps of diffusion after adding noise on the input latent. You can adjust the noise seed and the sampler/guider used in this diffusion stage. The original image is used here again for conditioning, if you entered one.

nodes.title: Decode
widgets_values:
## Decode

Make sure to adjust the number of tiles and overlap to fit your hardware.
(fewer tiles will result in faster execution, but will require more memory).

### Recommended settings

| node settings (pixels)                     | resolved latent geometry        |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------- |
| `512 / 64 / 128 / 32`                      | 16x16, ov 2 - 16f ov 4 |
| `768 / 192 / 128 / 32`                     | 24x24, ov 6 - 16f ov 4 |
| `1024 / 256 / 128 / 48`                    | 32x32, ov 8 - 16f, ov 6         |
| `1536 / 384 / 192 / 48`                    | 48x48, ov 12 - 24f, ov 6        |
| `768 / 192 / spatial-only`                 | 24x24, ov 6 - no temporal split |

nodes.title: Inputs
widgets_values:
## Inputs

Everything here is optional.

### Prompt

Enter a positive prompt. To rewrite it into a fuller description first, enable
**enhance positive prompt** on the Input Parameters node below. The negative
prompt is used as written and is never enhanced.

Supplying an **LTX API key** encodes and enhances the prompt through the API
instead of locally, which saves memory. The workflow switches over on its own
whenever a key is present - there is nothing to un-bypass.

See the [prompting guide](https://docs.ltx.io/open-source-model/usage-guides/prompting-guide).

### Image input

Condition the video to open on a still by loading an image and enabling
**use image input** on the Input Parameters node.

### Reference video

Turns the reference video into a control signal through an **annotator**.
**Depth** is wired by default; open the Reference Video node to switch to
**Canny** or **Pose**.

Its width, height, length and frame rate drive the whole generation: the fps
feeds both the text conditioning and Preprocess. The union-control **IC-LoRA**
is loaded in **Load Models**, and the guide frames are injected in
**Preprocess**, then cropped out after stage 1.

nodes.title: Generate - stage 1
widgets_values:
## Generate - stage 1

**Sampler - Distilled (8 steps)**

This is the flow for the first stage. It takes the distilled ltx-2.5 model with the union ic-lora LoRA applied on top of it and runs the diffusion in 8 steps. You can change the noise seed, the guider cfg (used for both video and audio) and select the sampler.

nodes.title: Preprocess
widgets_values:
## Preprocess

Builds the empty audio-video latent at the **reference video's** size and length, conditions on the optional start image, sets the conditioning frame-rate from the reference fps, and injects the reference **guide frames** via the IC-LoRA (`LTXAddVideoICLoRAGuide`).

The guide frames are cropped out after stage 1 (`LTXVCropGuides`) so stage 2 upscales only the generated video.

groups.title: Load Models - one file per output
Input Image - pass only if use_image
Prompt Text Encode via API for more memory efficient run

widgets_values: Do explore various samplers and cfg values (although we advise them to be kept close to 1)

nodes.title: Reference video → control signal
widgets_values:
## Reference control signal

The reference video is turned into a guide by an **annotator**. **Depth** (VideoDepthAnything) is wired by default.

## To switch:

connect **Canny** (`CannyEdgePreprocessor`) or **Pose** (`DWPreprocessor`) output into the `input` of the *scale-to-multiple* Resize node instead of the Depth output. All three read the resized reference frames; only the one wired into that Resize is used.
